title: Toroczkai's independent-edge conjecture for prime gap graphs
statement:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime number, with $p_0=1$. A **prime gap graph** on $n$ vertices is a simple graph whose vertex degrees are $p_1-p_0,\dotsc,p_n-p_{n-1}$; two edges are **independent** when they have no common vertex. **Toroczkai's independent-edge conjecture.** In every prime gap graph on $n$ vertices, there exist

$$
\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{2}
$$

independent edges. The supplied context does not state whether this assertion has been proved or remains open.
source_name: Péter L. Erdős, Gergely Harcos, Shubha R. Kharel, Péter Maga, Tamás R. Mezei and Zoltán Toroczkai, “The sequence of prime gaps is graphic”, arXiv:2205.00580 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).
